items.title: Recognize managed global-thin projects as activity-log writable roots
items.context: The heartbeat child process can run session_brief in a global-thin project, but cli-engine writeLog currently gates activity logging on hasProjectConfigFile(), whose config filename set only includes lattice.config.json. Add an explicit helper for runtime/log root detection that accepts .lattice/lattice.json with assetMode global-thin without teaching loadConfig() to parse that file as canonical project config.

happy.desc: A managed global-thin project with .lattice/lattice.json declaring assetMode=global-thin and no lattice.config.json runs a heartbeat/log-producing read-only command and writes a current row to that project root .lattice/activity.jsonl. WHY: proves runtime activity-root detection accepts the managed global-thin manifest.

edge.desc: The global-thin runtime/log-root helper remains separate from canonical configuration loading: loadConfig/findProjectRoot behavior still requires lattice.config.json for canonical project config fields and does not parse .lattice/lattice.json as a substitute project config. WHY: prevents managed adapter metadata from becoming canonical workflow config.

adversarial.desc: Directories with no lattice.config.json and no valid managed global-thin .lattice/lattice.json, including malformed or wrong-assetMode manifests, are not promoted to writable activity roots and do not gain stray .lattice/activity.jsonl logs. WHY: prevents unrelated directories from becoming Proofbound roots accidentally.

items.title: Cover canonical and global-thin activity logging behavior with regression tests
items.context: Add focused regression or smoke coverage proving canonical lattice.config.json projects still log activity, global-thin managed projects log activity, and unrelated directories do not become project roots accidentally.
